country: Multinational (12 hospitals worldwide; BraTS 2021 plus clinical data)

links.outcome: Segmentation performance with missing MRI sequences using sparsified training
links.effect: With Sparsified training, missing MRI sequences did not statistically affect performance; nn-Unet gave accurate segmentations despite incomplete MRI datasets.
links.quote: By applying Sparsified training, missing MRI sequences did not statistically affect the performance.

links.outcome: Performance on external test set from other hospitals versus internal test set
links.effect: All models' median DSC on both internal and external test sets were within or above human inter-rater agreement (0.74-0.85); nn-Unet DSC internal 0.86, external 0.93.
links.quote: All models' median Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) for both test sets were within, or higher than, previously reported human inter-rater agreement (range of 0.74-0.85).

unlisted_practices: Sparsified training to make segmentation models robust to missing MRI sequences

screen.reason: Evaluates generalizability and robustness of deep learning segmentation models across multi-center clinical MRI datasets with missing sequences, but does not test organizational deployment practices or safeguards.
